titel: The Psychology Of Success | Guy Raz

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen (Abruf laeuft ueber den Werbedienst podtrac.com) - zu wenig fuer ein Urteil, aber nicht nichts

einzeiler: Guy Raz on the psychology of success, learning from failure, and embracing discomfort.
kurzfassung: Guy Raz joins the podcast to discuss the hidden psychology behind professional success and why failure is often an essential prerequisite for growth. He reflects on his early career rejections, the evolution of his podcasting journey, and the importance of finding a sustainable pace rather than chasing endless scale. The conversation also explores the role of luck, privilege, and building meaningful relationships amidst the demands of work.
stichpunkte: Guy Raz started his media career facing continuous rejections before landing an unexpected internship at NPR.
Failure is framed not as a permanent setback, but as a painful yet necessary building block for future growth.
Transitioning from traditional journalism to podcasting allowed Raz to build successful shows like How I Built This.
Historical examples like Brunelleschi and Michelangelo show that career detours often lead to true masterpieces.
Luck and unearned privilege play significant roles in success, alongside internal resilience and perseverance.
Endless business scaling can lead to burnout, prompting some founders to prioritize sustainable operations instead.
Strong personal relationships and a supportive marriage often outweigh professional achievements as sources of life fulfillment.

clips.hook: A reporter's notebook as a superpower.
clips.text: Carrying a recording tool granted the speaker a sense of confidence and a valid reason to interact with anyone without feeling personally exposed.

clips.hook: The clunky early days of podcasting.
clips.text: The early format required listeners to manually connect portable media players to desktop hardware just to retrieve audio files.

clips.hook: Kids get bored even in ancient Rome.
clips.text: Teenage children on a family sightseeing tour grew tired of historical landmarks and simply wanted to wander around the city streets normally.

clips.hook: Timing a romance right before a major move.
clips.text: The guest met his future spouse at a social gathering merely weeks before relocating overseas for a multi-year assignment.

clips.hook: A remarkably modest and happy lifestyle.
clips.text: An elderly mother thrives with minimal monthly expenses, finding complete contentment through active daily habits and community ties.

beschreibung:
A podcast pioneer on failure, resilience, luck, work/life balance, and the power of questions.
Guy Raz has been instrumental in creating some of the most iconic podcasts in the world, including Wondery's How I Built This, Wow in the World and TED Radio Hour. The New York Times has described him as "one of the most popular podcasters in history."
We talk about:
The challenge – and gift – of failure
Getting comfortable with discomfort and risk
The notion of luck
The balance between your relationships and your work
Why scale isn't always the answer
Success vs. happiness
And much more
